data.narrative: Devanshi demonstrated exceptional skill in vertical slice decomposition and scope boundary control. Formulated 5 incrementally ordered vertical slices from an ultra-thin walking skeleton to complete escrow workflows. Successfully defended against late-breaking stakeholder scope creep by proposing an isolated Slice 1.5 payment feasibility spike, eliminating delivery risk while fulfilling investor requirements.

dimension_scores.observation: Extracted crisp scopes and explicit anti-scopes distinguishing core marketplace mechanics from secondary concerns like search, auth, and multi-currency billing.
Structured slices in a strict forward-building dependency DAG (Slice 1 -> Slice 2 -> Slice 3 -> Slice 4 -> Slice 5).
Recognized high integration risks in external payment gateways and avoided entangling third-party APIs into the initial core booking validation loop.
Crafted unambiguous, human-verifiable acceptance criteria that non-technical stakeholders and engineers can execute without checking database internals.
Quickly adapted to the 11th-hour investor demo request by scoping a decoupled Slice 1.5 payment spike rather than bloated monolithic refactoring.
dimension_scores.evidence: Authored PM trade-off message in progress/decomposition/module-04-fix.md.

dimension_scores.observation: Balanced end-to-end user interface fidelity with technical feasibility, selecting demand-side walking skeleton to test core product hypothesis immediately.

strengths: Rigorous anti-scope definitions that prevent stakeholder misalignment and scope creep
Human-verifiable clickthrough acceptance criteria testing product viability
Principled scope negotiation offering decoupled technical spikes over uncalculated overtime
